title: A screen reader cannot name the watch's big Done and Go buttons, and a greyed Done is not read at all
what: The big round Done button (a tick) and Go button (an arrow) show only a picture with no spoken name, so a screen reader user hears a button with no word. While Done cannot be used yet, it is not a button at all for the screen reader, and only its grey colour tells a sighted member it is off.
expected: Done and Go are read as 'Done, log this set' and 'Next exercise', and a Done that cannot be used yet is read as 'Done, not available'.
how_often: every set logged on the watch with a screen reader on
fix_line: Give the tick and arrow buttons a spoken name and keep the greyed Done as a button marked not available

title: Several watch buttons are much smaller than a finger
what: The screen is drawn on a 456-point plan scaled to the watch (about 0.42 to 0.5 finger units per point). 'Not now' is 46 points tall (about 21 units), 'Allow' and 'Open on phone' 52 points (about 24), the effort number tiles 64 points tall (about 29) and the effort Skip 80 points (about 36). Wear OS asks for at least 48.
expected: Every button on the watch is at least 48 finger units tall and wide, or has a touch area that big around it.
how_often: first launch, and every effort rating
fix_line: Make the touch area of these buttons at least 48 finger units, even where the drawn shape stays small

title: Most watch screens ignore the member's larger text setting
what: Words on the permission, no workout, workout saved, get the phone app, phone not connected and rest screens are drawn at one fixed size whatever text size the member chose. Only some words on the logging screens grow, and those stop at 1.24 times.
expected: Words grow with the member's text size (the big numbers may stay fixed), with the layout made to fit at the largest setting.
how_often: every time, for members with large text on
fix_line: Let the words on every watch screen grow with the text size setting, keeping only the big numbers fixed

title: 'Not now' on the watch's first screens looks like plain words
what: Under the filled Allow button, 'Not now' is white text with no outline or fill, so a first-time member cannot tell it is a button.
expected: 'Not now' has a visible outline or fill so it reads as a button.
fix_line: Draw 'Not now' as an outlined button

title: After 'Not now', the watch never offers heart rate or rest alerts again
what: Tapping 'Not now' on the heart rate or rest alerts screen hides it for good. The watch app has no other place to turn these on, and the heart rate line simply disappears, so the member is never told why or where to switch it on.
expected: A way back stays: for example a small 'Heart rate off, tap to turn on' line or a later reminder, so the member can still get what 'Not now' put off.
how_often: every member who taps Not now once
fix_line: Show a small tap-to-turn-on line where the heart rate would be, and offer rest alerts again later
